A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same benchmark and Anchor detector. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: V2 reports original detector evaluations, editing experiments, prompt-sensitivity analyses, runtime measurements, and comparisons of human and AI reviews.

after.justification: V3 retains those original results and adds mixed-authorship, agent-pipeline, embedding-sensitivity, classifier-training, and diagnostic experiments.

M1.justification: Anchor retains manuscript-conditioned reference generation, embedding cosine similarity, calibrated thresholds, and any-positive voting across anchor LLMs (Equations 1–5 and Appendix D.1). Alternative embeddings are evaluated as sensitivity tests; the proposed detection procedure is unchanged.

E1.justification: The core ICLR/NeurIPS dataset remains unchanged, but v3 adds reviews from AI Scientist, AgentReview, and DeepReview pipelines (Appendix D.3). Section 5.3 also adds a distinct mixed-authorship scenario: GPT-4.1 expands bullet points derived from human reviews. These substantially extend the evaluated generation conditions and authorship scenarios.

E2.justification: The original detector comparisons retain their comparator membership. Appendix D.9 and Table S16 add a focused comparator family: RoBERTa classifiers fine-tuned separately on GPT-4o, Gemini, and Claude peer reviews, with comparisons to Anchor. The agent-based reviewing systems supply evaluation texts rather than additional detectors.

E3.justification: Existing splits and low-FPR calibration procedures are retained. Added experiments introduce AUROC evaluation of agent-generated reviews against ICLR 2022 human controls, two-stage GPT-4.1 generation for 500 mixed-authorship reviews, enriched-prompt controls, alternative embedding configurations, and same-source/cross-source classifier evaluation. Appendix D.11 also introduces GPT-4.1 judging of 500 reviews.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained archetype-prompt, editing, and score analyses, v3 tests robustness to structured generation pipelines and enriched prompts, sensitivity to embedding choice, and the effect of domain-specific classifier training. Appendices D.10–D.11 add topic-distribution analysis and investigation of whether identifiable review deficiencies track detection success.

E5.justification: New Table S11 reports bootstrap means, minima, and maxima with n=1,000. The existing 100-resample standard deviations in Table S5, 20 runtime repetitions, and Wilcoxon tests remain unchanged. This adds uncertainty reporting for another experiment without establishing increased repetition of the original experiments.

E6.justification: Retained tables and figure data are unchanged, but substantial results are added. Table 4 reports Anchor TPRs of 5.8–18.6% for bullet-point-derived reviews, at actual FPRs of 0.2–2.2%. Table S11 reports pipeline-review AUROCs of 0.9929–0.9985. Tables S13, S15, and S16 add prompt, embedding, and trained-classifier results; D.10–D.11 add diagnostic findings. These are new evaluations, not improvements to the retained benchmark scores.

T1.justification: Equations 1–5 retain the same mathematical definitions and decision rule. Neither version supplies additional theorems, proofs, or substantive formal derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory contribution list, and conclusion retain the same substantive claims about the dataset, existing detectors' limitations, manuscript context, AI-review characteristics, and editing detectability. New experiments expand supporting evidence without redefining these headline contributions.

C2.justification: V3 adds interpretations concerning legitimate writing assistance, robustness to agentic and enriched prompting, embedding dependence, and supervised classifiers' generalization. Appendix D.11 proposes explanations for the lack of association between recognizable review deficiencies and detection success; the ethics statement discusses obstacles to studying real users' prompts. The original limitations are retained in Appendix F.

D1.justification: V3 supplies bullet-point and enrichment prompts, alternative embedding identifiers, and additional experiment-specific implementation information. It also states that edited reviews are included in the release. However, B.1 replaces the explicit dataset license/access description with a supplementary subset and promised future release, conflicting with the abstract and Appendix I's public-release statements. Actual withdrawal or licensing changes cannot be established from the PDFs.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds focused differentiation of Anchor from the already cited DetectLLM and DNA-GPT. New references cover AI Scientist, DeepReview, writing-assistant design, and Jina/e5 embeddings. The broader literature framing is retained; the conversion to author-year citations is principally a presentation change.

P1.justification: The Anchor description moves from Section 5.1 to Section 4.1, preceding baseline evaluation, while limitations move from Section 6 to Appendix F. Focused prose expansions, updated affiliations, and revised heading/citation styles accompany largely retained wording rather than extensive rewriting.

P2.justification: V3 adds Table 4 and Tables S11, S13, S15, and S16, substantially expanding the result displays. It adopts an ICLR layout, reformats the directory listing and Anchor equations, and redistributes existing tables and figures. The retained figure graphics themselves are unchanged.

improvement.justification: The added embedding-sensitivity and benchmark-trained classifier experiments examine dependencies left untested in v2, while expanded generation and mixed-authorship tests clarify applicability. These strengthen the evidence, but the agent-pipeline evaluation reports only Binoculars AUROC, leaving stringent-FPR behavior unresolved, and the new classifier training setup lacks important reproducibility details. Conflicting dataset-release statements also weaken documentation. The evidence supports a useful but limited net improvement.
